cohort: Pregnant women with rheumatic heart disease receiving care at a single center between 2011 and 2021
finding: Atrial fibrillation in pregnancy among women with rheumatic heart disease was associated with an increased risk of maternal morbidity and mortality, and a trend towards an increased risk of some non-cardiac pregnancy complications.
mod_finding: Women with atrial fibrillation had higher rates of cesarean delivery compared to those without atrial fibrillation (31.9% vs. 18.3%).
